draft.title: Gustatory perception
card: Gustatory perception is the sense of taste. Taste receptors on the tongue detect chemicals in food and send signals to the brain.
The brain combines those signals with smell, texture and sight to build the flavour of a food. This is why food can seem bland when a person has a blocked nose.
factors such as genes, age and the number of taste receptors a person has can change how strongly they taste.
factors such as past experience, mood, expectations, culture and family eating habits also shape what a person likes and how a food tastes.
draft.remember: Flavour is built by the brain from taste, smell, texture and sight, and shaped by many factors.

a.q: Why does food often seem bland to a person with a blocked nose?
opts: Smell signals that help build flavour are reduced
The taste receptors on the tongue stop working
Texture is no longer detected by the mouth
The brain stops using signals from taste receptors
a.why: Flavour is built by combining taste receptor signals with smell. A blocked nose reduces the smell input, so flavour is weaker. The tongue's receptors still send signals, so the second option is wrong.
a.clue: Flavour uses more than the tongue.

b.q: Tariq grew up eating very spicy food at family meals and now enjoys chilli that his classmate Jo finds unpleasant. Which factor best explains the difference?
opts: Past experience and family habits shape his response
Jo has fewer taste receptors than Tariq has
Chilli sends signals only to the smell system
Tariq's tongue detects chemicals that Jo's cannot
b.why: Tariq's family eating habits and repeated experience are social and psychological factors that shape how he responds to chilli. The receptor option is tempting, but nothing in the case says the two differ in receptors, and the card says many factors shape taste.
b.clue: Look at how Tariq grew up, not at his tongue.

a.best: Smell signals that help build flavour are reduced

b.best: Past experience and family habits shape his response

problems.detail: The clue 'Look at how Tariq grew up, not at his tongue' rules out both receptor options and points straight to the upbringing option. A student can answer without understanding psychological and social factors.
